statutory_anchors_reverified_2026_10_23.authority: 15 U.S.C. § 295 (National Gold and Silver Stamping Act — Standard of fineness of gold articles; deviation)
statutory_anchors_reverified_2026_10_23.verbatim_summary: Actual fineness of gold or alloy shall not be less by more than three one-thousandths parts (3/1000) than the fineness indicated by the mark on any unsoldered part, and not less by more than seven one-thousandths parts (7/1000) when tested as a whole including all solder and alloyed inferior metal (for post-1981 articles).

statutory_anchors_reverified_2026_10_23.authority: 15 U.S.C. § 297(b) (Identifying trademark required alongside quality mark)
statutory_anchors_reverified_2026_10_23.verbatim_summary: Whenever a quality mark is stamped or applied to any gold or silver article, the person, firm, corporation, or association must also apply a trademark duly registered or applied for under U.S. law (or its legal name) closely accompanying the quality mark in type or lettering at least as large as the quality mark.

statutory_anchors_reverified_2026_10_23.authority: 16 CFR Part 23 (FTC Guides for the Jewelry, Precious Metals, and Pewter Industries, current as of 2026-10-21)
statutory_anchors_reverified_2026_10_23.verbatim_summary: § 23.3(a)-(b) restricts unqualified 'Gold' to 24 karat fine gold and requires karat disclosure below 24K; § 23.3(c)(1) & fn. 32 prohibit describing any hollow-center article as 'Solid Gold'; § 23.4 defines 'Vermeil' as ≥2.5 microns of ≥10K gold over sterling silver; § 23.10 reiterates mandatory maker trademark beside quality marks; § 23.18 sets 1 metric carat = 200 mg (0.20 g).
